title: A Policy That Is a Straight Line: Least Squares on the Demonstrations, the Gains It Finds, and the Limit It Cannot Fit

questions.question: Why fit a straight-line policy before a network?
options: A network cannot be fitted until a line has been
A line is always more accurate than a network
It is the baseline: a network that does no better has learned nothing the line did not
A line needs no data
questions.explanation: The line costs one solve and no tuning, and its error is the number every more complex learner has to beat.

questions.question: From demonstrations that never reached the car's limit, what did least squares find?
options: The expert's own gains, -2.000 and -3.000
Gains about half the expert's
Zero, since the data had no noise
questions.explanation: Within its linear range the expert is a straight line, and the fit recovered it with an error of 0.000000.

questions.question: With 8.4 percent of the actions at the limit, what did the line do?
options: It found the expert's gains again
Its weights shrank to -1.044 and -1.576 and an error of 0.01816 was left
It failed to solve
It fitted the limit exactly
questions.explanation: A line cannot stop growing where the expert's turn does. The best line is a compromise that is wrong at both ends.

questions.question: A ridge of 100 was added. What happened?
options: The error fell
The constant was pulled to zero
The weights grew
The weights shrank to -0.592 and -0.614 and the error rose to 0.04677
questions.explanation: The ridge trades error for steadiness. It is worth it with few or collinear samples, not here.

questions.question: Why does fit_linear give the zero policy for a set in which one state was seen ten times?
options: Ten samples are too few for any fit
The normal equations are singular: one state cannot fix two weights and a constant
The ridge was zero
Zero is the least squares answer for one state
questions.explanation: With no variation in the features, many lines fit equally well. Returning one of them as if it were learned would be a guess.

questions.question: How should the ridge be chosen?
options: By its error on a validation set kept apart from the test set
As large as possible
By its error on the test set
Always zero
questions.explanation: A ridge chosen on the test set makes the test set part of the training, the leak of 38-01 in another form.
